source_refs.note: Exercise 10.1, Question 7: book page 278 (Q1-Q24). The book prints no answers for Exercise 10.1.

blocks.prompt: 7 Solve the following trigonometric equation: \(\sqrt{2}\cos x\sin x - \sin x = 0\)
blocks.explanation:
Both terms contain \(\sin x\): take it out as a common factor (do not cancel it).
This gives \(\sin x = 0\) or \(\cos x = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\).
Plan: solve both basic equations in \([0, 2\pi]\) and write their families.
steps:
Given: \(\sqrt{2}\cos x\sin x - \sin x = 0\).
To find: principal solutions and general solution.
Method: factorise by taking \(\sin x\) common, then set each factor to zero.

Take \(\sin x\) common
\[\sin x\left(\sqrt{2}\cos x - 1\right) = 0\]
\[\sin x = 0\ \text{ or }\ \cos x = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\]
Why: a product is zero only when a factor is zero. Dividing by \(\sin x\) instead would lose the solutions with \(\sin x = 0\).

When \(\sin x = 0\)
\[x = 0,\ \pi,\ 2\pi\]
in \([0, 2\pi]\); in general \(x = n\pi\).
Why: sine is zero at both ends of the horizontal diameter of the unit circle, i.e. at every multiple of \(\pi\).

When \(\cos x = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\)
Cosine is positive: quadrants I and IV, reference angle \(\frac{\pi}{4}\).
\[x = \dfrac{\pi}{4}\]
\[x = 2\pi - \dfrac{\pi}{4} = \dfrac{7\pi}{4}\]
Why: \(\cos\frac{\pi}{4} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\).

General solution
\[\left\{n\pi\right\}\]
\[\cup \left\{\dfrac{\pi}{4} + 2n\pi\right\}\]
\[\cup \left\{\dfrac{7\pi}{4} + 2n\pi\right\},\ n \in \mathbb{Z}\]
Why: \(\{n\pi\}\) collects \(0 + 2n\pi\) and \(\pi + 2n\pi\) together; the cosine values repeat after \(2\pi\).

Check
\[x = \dfrac{\pi}{4}:\ \sqrt{2}\cdot\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\cdot\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} = 0\]
Why: \(\sin\frac{\pi}{4} = \cos\frac{\pi}{4} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\). At \(x = n\pi\) both terms contain \(\sin x = 0\).

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: The textbook prints no answers for Exercise 10.1. Every answer on this page is ours: worked out step by step, checked independently with a computer algebra system (sympy) and compared with a solution book. As in the book's examples, we give the principal solutions in \([0, 2\pi]\) and the general solution as a union of sets.
